chunks: It is not for a prophet to be false; and whoever is false will indeed bring his falsehood with him on the Day of Reckoning when each will receive his reward without favour or wrong.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a prophet to 'be false' or 'be deceitful' in the context of Surah Aal Imran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as establishing the infallibility (Ismah) of the Prophets, particularly Imam Ali, by negating the possibility of them concealing or misappropriating divine knowledge (Ghul). The term 'yaghul' implies a secret taking or hoarding, suggesting that Prophets do not hide any part of the revelation they were entrusted to convey. This reinforces the concept that the Prophet's teachings are complete and unadulterated, ensuring the integrity of the message delivered to the community.
